about: D4: is a [monitoring-critical] alert explained by known maintenance or a transient outage? Advisory only.
ask: The state is a critical alert raised by the software-factory watcher: `alert_class` (what failed), `cause` (the bounded error text), and `utc_time` (when it fired, HH:MM UTC). Is this alert EXPECTED, meaning it is fully explained by known maintenance or a transient outage that clears on its own, so no one needs to act? Known maintenance: Forgejo (Forge) stops for about 4 minutes every night for its backup, starting 03:17 UTC, so a Forgejo timeout, connection refused or reset, HTTP 502/503/504, or a lane with no postings, fired between 03:10 and 03:35 UTC, is expected. A cause that itself says maintenance, a planned restart, or a deploy in progress is expected at any time. A defect, database, authentication, or config error is never expected, even inside the maintenance window or when the cause also mentions maintenance: that rule wins over every expected case. Answer no for anything else: a code defect (TypeError, undefined, cannot read properties, a parse, schema, or validation error), a database or SQL error, an authentication or permission failure (401, 403, permission denied, token), an invalid config, a timeout or outage outside the maintenance window, or anything you cannot explain as maintenance.
